chunks: So (they were punished) for breaking the covenant and disbelieving the signs of God, and for killing the prophets unjustly, and saying: "Our hearts are enfolded in covers," (though) in fact God had sealed them because of their unbelief; so they do not believe except a few;
ai.seo_question: What are the reasons for the punishment of the Children of Israel mentioned in Surah An-Nisa?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the specific covenant of the Children of Israel and their rejection of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Imam Ali (AS), illustrating the transition from divine seal to human agency. The phrase 'hearts were envelopes' (ghulfun) is interpreted as their self-imposed spiritual blindness, which God then confirmed as a consequence of their persistent disbelief. This highlights the principle that divine sealing of the heart is a result of accumulated human actions rather than arbitrary predestination.
